column1: # What build/check-upstream.sh watches, and the single source of truth for it.
# The script (shared verbatim across every repository in these families) knows how to query each
# ecosystem but nothing about which components matter here. This repository binds nothing native,
# and deliberately does not watch the Salesforce SDKs: MarketingCloudSDK.Net.Android and
# MarketingCloudSDK.Net.iOS already do that, each for the platform it binds. Watching them here as
# well would file the same native release as an issue in three repositories at once.
# What this repository watches instead is the one thing nothing else can see: the packages it pins
# by hand, by exact version, in Directory.Build.props. That is both platform bindings and the
# SFMCSDK.Net core umbrella, which sits underneath this one and moves on its own release train.
# When any of them publishes, this façade keeps resolving the older package until somebody
# re-pins it, and nothing said so.
# The `nuget` check is deliberately asymmetric: a pin BEHIND nuget.org is a finding (re-pin here),
# a pin AHEAD of it is the normal mid-flight state of a release train (the platform repositories
# publish first, then SFMCSDK.Net, then this one) and is only logged. A prerelease pin is always
# reported.
# Columns are single-tab-separated.
#   group    reporting group - one GitHub issue per group, titled with this text
#   label    how the component is named inside the issue
#   kind     cocoapods | maven | github-release | github-tag | nuget
#   pin      the MSBuild property in Directory.Build.props holding the pinned version
#   locator  kind-specific: pod name, groupId:artifactId[:packaging][@repo], owner/repo, or the
#            NuGet package id
#   confirm  download URL template with {version}, or "-" to derive it from the locator
#   source   owner/repo publishing the component - optional, and only meaningful on nuget
#            rows, where the drift finding links that repository's release notes for the
#            version it reports
# group
